# generator-shortcuts — 0d1deab2505c

## Strongest canonical-fitting rival

Replace each creature's actual tail with the fixed canonical artwork: two straight
stem cells and two diagonal terminal tips. Otherwise perform the correct
wall-directed translation and 180-degree arm-color turn. The executable declaration
is canonical_tail_template. It fits all 8 usable labeled canonical pair appearances
(four unique inputs), because every canonical tail has exactly that artwork.
The dynamic fit table in checks/transport-probe-final-retry/report.json verifies
that claim, rather than assuming that an arbitrary wrong rule is canonical-fitting.

## Exact counterexample

Input: 9 rows x 11 columns. Output: 9 rows x 11 columns.
Coordinates are zero-based. The center is (4,3); its three-cell straight tail is at
(4,5), (4,6), (4,7). The whole creature moves two columns left. Its tail retains
those three straight cells after translation; the arm colors turn 180 degrees.

Input:

    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
    [8,8,8,2,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
    [8,8,3,4,7,1,1,1,8,8,8]
    [8,8,8,6,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]

Actual canonical Racket output:

    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]

    [8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]

Rival output:

The Racket output and independently placed expected grid agree. The input passes
the repaired self_check with no findings. Exact differing coordinates, labels,
source hashes and runnable reproduction are retained in
repo/generators/0d1deab2505c/counterexamples/canonical_tail_template.json.

## How the output was checked

The reusable workspace/probe_transport.py makes the fixture by explicit placement,
independently calculates its expected destination cells, and obtains the actual
selected canonical label through public Catalog.apply. The successful five-case
receipt is checks/transport-probe-final-retry/racket.json; the source-bound comparison
and dynamic rival results are in report.json alongside it. Generator SHA-256:
24b57d0c9c06922e455ca7e97cef32a520e835c3a1cba6d036c20e809122764d. Canonical program-text SHA-256: f797a23338ff7a811630e577417a3f8008a502fa73214d466709b0c9713b71e8.

The earlier resource-interrupted attempt is preserved separately and does not
supply this successful label. A missing Racket output is classified as a reference
error by the final probe.

## Does the repaired generator emit such cases?

Yes. Noncanonical ordinary phases vary the first creature's tail length and force
a different second tail, so they distinguish actual transport from both the fixed
canonical template and the further shortcut of copying the first creature's tail
to all creatures. A fully reproducible generated case is also in the five-case
probe: seed 0, sample_index 1, medium, grid_h 12, grid_w 15, creature_count 2,
tail_direction right, tail_length 3, tail_branch false, palette_size 10.
That exact emitted input and its actual Racket/rival outputs are retained there.

The 9x11 grid above is hand-authored; this report does not claim that exact placement
was observed in an unpinned draw. The completed production census used 100 lessons
per band, three demonstrations and one query: all 300 lessons and all 1,200 held-out
rotations refuted the declared canonical-tail and copy-first-tail shortcuts.
Every declared cyclic start was additionally checked at seed 0: 9 lessons and 36
rotations, with 14 unique inputs. These finite results cover five distinct declared
rivals and do not prove unique induction against arbitrary programs.
